posts.content:
LG Electronics Water Science Research Center Earns “Laboratory of Excellence” Certification

from ERA’s 2025 International Proficiency Testing Program



LG Electronics’ Water Science Research Center, which provides ongoing water quality analysis services to ensure customers can scientifically verify the water they drink every day at home or in the office, has been awarded the “Laboratory of Excellence” certification by the U.S.-based Environmental Resource Associates (ERA) in its 2025 International Proficiency Testing Program.

The center successfully passed evaluations across 24 testing parameters, including not only the standard 17 items but also additional assessments for heavy metals such as lead, arsenic, and chloroform, as well as minerals that affect water hardness like calcium, magnesium, and fluoride. All items received a “satisfactory” rating.

Recognized for its strong analytical capabilities and validated data, LG’s Water Science Research Center has held international accreditation as a KOLAS-certified testing laboratory since 2015.

Founded in 1977, ERA is a globally recognized proficiency testing organization accredited by both the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO/IEC). ERA’s annual proficiency testing covers six categories—water quality, drinking water, water microbiology, persistent pollutants, soil, and air—with more than 6,000 laboratories from over 80 countries participating worldwide.

LG Electronics also demonstrated its expertise in hygiene-related testing by earning satisfactory results in total coliforms and E. coli from the Food Analysis Performance Assessment Scheme (FAPAS), a proficiency program administered by the U.K. Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (DEFRA). FAPAS is globally recognized by the European Union (EU) and food safety regulators across the world.

Water Quality Analysis Service for LG Water Purifier Customers

LG Electronics provides its water purifier customers with an easy-to-access water quality analysis consultation service. Customers can request the service through the LGE.com website by searching keywords such as “water analysis,” “water test,” or “water quality”, as well as through the Customer Support section or by phone consultation.

posts.content:
Worried About Microplastics in Your Water? LG Has the Answer


LG Electronics has introduced a new ice water purifier equipped with a microplastic filtering system, designed to protect families from invisible contaminants in their drinking water.

While many people rely on bottled water or conventional purifiers, studies have shown that these methods do not prevent microplastics from entering the body. Research from Columbia University’s Earth Institute revealed that between 110,000 and 370,000 plastic particles can be found in just one liter of bottled water. About 90% are nanoplastics, which are so small—measured in billionths of a meter—that they can penetrate deep into organs and tissues.

Experts warn that nanoplastics may damage brain tissue, disrupt capillaries in hands and feet, and release harmful additives such as Bisphenol A (BPA) and phthalates, which are known hormone disruptors. The World Health Organization (WHO) has also raised concerns that microplastics may trigger long-term inflammation in the body and bind to microbes that can cause infections.

In response to these growing concerns, LG Electronics has launched the LG PuriCare Objet Collection Ice Water Purifier, which features the All-Puri Filter System. This advanced filter removes 99.8% of microplastics and 99.99% of noroviruses, ensuring cleaner and safer drinking water.

The purifier also comes with UVnano sterilization technology, which automatically disinfects the water outlet, ice maker, and ice dispenser by 99.9%. Additionally, its high-temperature pipe sterilization function cleanses internal water pipes weekly, eliminating bacteria such as E. coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

For added assurance, customers can also opt for a premium care service, where a professional care manager visits the home to disassemble and clean the ice storage compartment, ensuring optimal hygiene.

An LG Electronics spokesperson said, “With rising concerns over microplastics, it is more important than ever to safeguard the safety of drinking water and ice at home. LG will continue to invest in advanced purification technologies to provide safer and cleaner water for families.”

posts.title: LG Expands Appliance Subscription Business
posts.excerpt: LG Electronics’ Subscription Business Gains Momentum, Eyes ₩2 Trillion in Revenue LG Electro
posts.content:
LG Electronics’ Subscription Business Gains Momentum, Eyes ₩2 Trillion in Revenue


LG Electronics’ home appliance subscription business is accelerating both at home and abroad. In Malaysia alone, subscription sales surpassed 10,000 units last month, and the company is now preparing to expand into Singapore. Building on this momentum, subscription revenue, which topped ₩1 trillion last year, is expected to approach ₩2 trillion (about USD 1.5 billion) this year.

According to industry sources on the 15th, LG achieved the 10,000-unit milestone in Malaysia since first introducing water purifier subscriptions there in 2019, later expanding to major appliances in 2023. In Singapore, LG began pilot subscription services in April and is currently testing consumer response before the official launch. The offering covers nine appliances—including refrigerators, washing machines, and water purifiers—with contract terms ranging from three to seven years.

Currently, LG operates subscription services in Taiwan and Thailand, while its pilot program in India ended in January after several months of testing. Analysts believe LG is refining its approach to better fit the Indian market before relaunching. The company plans to expand subscription services to additional regions as part of its long-term strategy.

The subscription model has become a key growth driver for LG Electronics. It lowers the upfront cost barrier for customers purchasing high-priced appliances, while also ensuring ongoing customer engagement through regular maintenance visits from LG service staff.

LG first entered the subscription market in 2009 with water purifier rentals. In 2022, it expanded to large appliances and now offers subscription options for over 300 products—covering nearly its entire appliance portfolio.

This strategy has delivered strong results: in Q1 2025, subscription revenue (excluding care services) reached ₩501 billion, up 45% from ₩345.6 billion a year earlier. With similar performance expected in Q2, annual subscription revenue could climb close to ₩2 trillion, compared to ₩1.67 trillion last year.

By shifting from one-time sales to recurring revenue, LG reduces profit volatility and secures stable long-term demand. As one securities analyst noted, “The high-margin subscription model will be a major growth engine for LG, backed by strong consumer demand and rapid adoption.”

posts.content:
LG Electronics’ Subscription Business Posts Record Q1 Growth


LG Electronics’ home appliance subscription business is growing at a remarkable pace, with first-quarter revenue nearly matching the company’s full-year performance from five years ago.

According to industry reports on the 28th, LG’s subscription business generated ₩560 billion (approx. USD 400 million) in Q1 2025, a 36% increase compared to the same period last year (₩410 billion). This figure is close to LG’s total subscription revenue for 2020 (₩591 billion). Considering that Q1 is typically the off-season for appliances, analysts expect LG’s annual subscription revenue to surpass ₩2 trillion (approx. USD 1.5 billion) for the first time this year.

LG’s subscription sales have been steadily rising: ₩640 billion in 2021, ₩734.4 billion in 2022, and ₩962.8 billion in 2023, before jumping to ₩1.67 trillion last year.

The rapid growth is fueled by differentiated care services and a wider product portfolio. LG first launched its subscription business in 2009 with water purifier rentals, then expanded to major appliances in 2022, driving accelerated growth.

Overseas expansion has also played a major role. Since entering Malaysia in 2019, LG has rolled out subscription services to Thailand and Taiwan, with plans to extend into Singapore, Hong Kong, and India. The company noted that even in its early expansion stage, overseas subscription sales are contributing an increasing share to overall revenue.

Samsung Electronics, a latecomer to the subscription market, is also moving quickly. The company launched its “AI Subscription Club” in December 2024 and began offering Galaxy smartphones under subscription in January. During the presales of the Galaxy S25 in February, one in five self-purchasing customers opted into the subscription program—an early sign of strong demand. Samsung’s Q1 subscription revenue is expected to be disclosed in its earnings announcement on the 30th.
